## ServiceSettings v0.1.2

The first public build of a one-page switchboard for the Windows services you actually care about. Add a service once — its display label and its real service name — and from then on it is a card with a switch: on starts it, off stops it. Instead of hunting for it in `services.msc`, you open one window, and every card shows the service's real state each time the window comes up.

## New

### A switch per service

- Each card owns a custom-drawn toggle: a real focusable checkbox under a styled slider, so <kbd>Space</kbd> flips it as well as the mouse.
- The switch reflects the service, not your last click. On launch, every card's status is queried with `sc query <name>` after the list renders, and the toggle is set from that answer.
- Running is decided by the four-digit state code (`4  RUNNING`), not by the word — `STOP_PENDING` and `START_PENDING` contain letters that a looser substring check would misread as "running".
- While a `net start` / `net stop` for that card is in flight, further clicks on it are ignored, so the switch cannot desynchronise from the service. Toggles are additionally debounced by 500 ms.

### Elevation without arguments

- The app checks whether it is already elevated with `fltmc`; if it is not, it relaunches itself through `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, so it does not need to be started "as administrator" by hand.
- Commands are executed through `cmd.exe /c`, and the renderer never touches the shell directly: the preload exposes exactly one call, `window.api.run(command)`, which maps to a single IPC channel.
- Because the whole process runs elevated, the commands it starts do too — which is what makes starting a Windows service actually work.

### Adding and deleting

- The `+` card opens a modal asking for the label the card should show and the Windows service name; empty values are rejected, and clicking the backdrop closes it.
- Deletion is deliberately awkward: resting the cursor on a card for five seconds reveals an `×`; leaving hides it again; the confirmation dialog asks for the label before the card and its stored record are removed.
- On a first run, before anything has been stored, the list holds one stand-in card (`mysql` pointing at the service `MySQL84`). It is not written to disk until you add or delete something, so it never becomes a permanent ghost entry.

### Storage

- Everything lives in IndexedDB (`TestDB`, object store `config`, key path `id`, a single record with id `1`); there is no fallback file and no hidden state elsewhere.
- Saves use `put` rather than `add`, because the record exists on every save after the first and `add` would throw a `ConstraintError`.

### Packaging

- electron-builder, with `build/` as the build-resources directory: the icon set lives in both `build/` and `resources/` so that packaging and the runtime window icon use the same artwork.
- The application now ships its own icon: a white rounded tile with a gear and two orange knobs, transparent outside the tile, as `.ico` (7 sizes) and `.png`. macOS icon assets were dropped — this build targets Windows services, and there is no macOS story for `sc.exe`.

## Fixes

- The first click of a session could throw because `shell` was used without being imported; it is imported now.
- The service list and the card renderer had drifted onto two different storage keys, so an existing list could be read back as empty. One key is used everywhere.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ServiceSettings-0.1.2-setup.exe` | NSIS installer, x64 — the app relaunches itself elevated on start, so no manual "run as administrator" |

## Notes

- Windows only in practice: the app drives `sc.exe`, `net.exe` and `fltmc`, and expects them to be present as they are on a stock Windows install. The Electron shell itself builds elsewhere, but there is nothing useful for it to do there.
- Stack: Electron 38 · electron-vite 4 · Vite 7 · plain ES modules and DOM (no UI framework) · IndexedDB · prettier + eslint.
